why: Pain is real, but its intensity is not a direct damage meter. Understanding why it can vary helps you respond with more useful information and less alarm.

slides.title: Pain Can Change
slides.content: Symptoms can change across a day even when there has been no new injury. This does not make the experience less real.

slides.title: The Whole Picture Matters
slides.content: Tissue and nerve information matters. Sleep, stress, illness, previous experience, expectations, activity, environment, and a sense of safety can also influence protection.

slides.title: Look for Patterns
slides.content: Instead of judging one pain score in isolation, notice what was happening before it changed and how function, confidence, and symptoms trend over time.

slides.title: Variation Is Information
slides.content: A change in symptoms can help you adjust the dose, timing, recovery, or strategy. It is not automatically proof of harm or failure.

slides.title: Do Not Ignore Warning Signs
slides.content: New trauma, progressive weakness, major neurological change, fever, unexplained illness, or other concerning symptoms still require appropriate assessment.

slides.title: Try This Today
slides.content: When symptoms change, record three things: what changed, what else was happening, and what helped you continue or recover.
